note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Cambodia: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: Cambodia has no personal income tax as such: a resident's monthly salary is taxed at 0% to KHR 1,500,000, 5% to 2,000,000, 10% to 8,500,000, 15% to 12,500,000 and 20% above; consulting income falls under tax on income instead.

sources.said: There is no personal income tax, per se , in Cambodia. Instead, a monthly salary tax is imposed on individuals who derive income from employment.

figures.finding: Salary tax is monthly: the employer files and pays by the 20th day after the month; employees file no annual return.

sources.said: Employees do not have to file an annual return.
The tax withheld must be paid to the tax authorities no later than 20 days after the end of the month in which the salaries were paid.

figures.finding: The employer pays 0.8% occupational risk and 2.6% healthcare to the NSSF; the pension contribution is 4% of the contributory wage in its first five years (2% employer, 2% employee), rising to 8% in years six to ten.

sources.said: The employer is required to contribute ORC equal to 0.8% of the monthly average wage of an employee to the NSSF’s designated bank account.

The healthcare contribution is required from both employers and employees at 1.3% (each) of the monthly average wage of employees. However, from 1 January 2018, the obligation to pay the contribution of healthcare as stated in the above paragraph shall be the full burden (100%) of the employer.
In the first five years, the pension contribution rate is 4% of the contributory wage of the worker/employee. The employer contributes 2%, while the other 2% comes from the worker/employee.

figures.finding: The employer deducts salary tax by the tax tables (PAYE); a payment for services to a resident not registered with a VAT invoice bears 15% final withholding, and royalties 15%.

sources.said: Employers must deduct salary tax from employees' salaries in accordance with the tax tables on a pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) basis.
Royalties: 15%. Rental: 10%. Services: 15% (except payments to a registered taxpayer and supported by a valid VAT invoice).

figures.finding: A non-resident's Cambodian salary is taxed at a flat, final 20%; any other Cambodian-source income paid to a non-resident, including for services performed in Cambodia, bears 14% withholding.

sources.said: Non-residents are taxed at a flat rate of 20%, which constitutes a final tax.
who pays any Cambodian-source income as defined under Article 33 of the Law on Taxation to a non-resident taxpayer must withhold tax at 14% of the amount paid.
Income from services performed in Cambodia.

figures.finding: VAT is 10% for entities in the self-declaration regime.

sources.said: VAT is applicable to self-declaration regime entities and is charged at 10% on the value of the supply of most goods and services.
